newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB says low Thunder Bay stocks could delay ships.
newsitem.headline: CWB says low Thunder Bay stocks could delay ships.

text.p: Low grain stocks in Thunder Bay elevators could lead to a delay in vessel loadings on the lower St. Lawrence River, the Canadian Wheat Board said Monday.

"As you can see from the vessel lineup at the East Coast, we're still relatively current with loading vessels and a wait of five days," CWB spokeswoman Rhea Yates said. "If the situation persists, we would expect to see more vessels waiting for longer periods, but now we're still current."
Three ships were waiting to load on the East Coast Friday with the longest wait at five days, Yates said.

Thunder Bay elevators on May 4 contained 370,500 tonnes of wheat, barley, oats, flax, rye and canola, 28.9 percent of their total capacity of 1.28 million tonnes, Canadian Grain Commission statistics show.
That compares to 474,200 tonnes in store at Thunder Bay, or 37 percent of capacity, on May 5, 1996.
On the West Coast earlier this year, the CWB faced C$15 million in demurrage fees for delays in loading vessels. That backlog was blamed in part on slow railway shipments.
Rail car unloads at Thunder Bay exceeded the industry-set delivery targets in the week of May 5 to May 11 with 3,119 hopper cars unloaded versus the target of 3,075, Yates said.
